answer.question: List the Houston-area hospitals (Harris, Fort Bend, Montgomery, Galveston and Brazoria counties) that have a 30-day pneumonia readmission rate, with county, ownership, overall star rating, the rate and the number of eligible discharges behind it. Leave out hospitals without a rate. Lowest rate first; break ties by hospital name.
answer.answer: The results include 35 Houston-area hospitals with a reported 30-day pneumonia readmission rate, ordered from lowest to highest; ties are by hospital name. Eligible discharges are shown as the count behind each rate. Sweeny Community Hospital has no overall star rating reported. […]
answer.sql: SELECT facility_name, county, hospital_ownership, overall_rating, measure_id, measure_name, score AS readmission_rate, denominator AS eligible_discharges FROM hq.v_tx_latest WHERE is_houston_area IS TRUE AND UPPER(measure_id) = UPPER('READM_30_PN') AND score IS NOT NULL ORDER BY score ASC, facility_name ASC LIMIT 200

answer.question: Which measures have no reported score for more than half of Texas hospitals? Break ties by measure ID.
answer.answer: These are the 25 measures with the highest percent missing among Texas hospitals; all have no score for more than half of the 467 hospitals. Measure names are shown as their first 60 characters. […]
answer.sql: WITH texas_hospitals AS (SELECT facility_id FROM hq.hospitals WHERE UPPER(state) = 'TX'), total AS (SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_hospitals FROM texas_hospitals), ranked_values AS (SELECT mv.facility_id, UPPER(mv.measure_id) AS measure_id, mv.score, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY mv.facility_id, UPPER(mv.measure_id) ORDER BY mv.period_end DESC NULLS LAST, mv.period_start DESC NULLS LAST, mv.id DESC) AS period_rank FROM hq.measure_values AS mv JOIN texas_hospitals AS th ON th.facility_id = mv.facility_id), scored AS (SELECT measure_id, COUNT(DISTINCT facility_id) FILTER(WHERE score IS NOT NULL) AS hospitals_with_score FROM ranked_values WHERE period_rank = 1 GROUP BY measure_id) SELECT m.measure_id, m.domain, LEFT(m.measure_name, 60) AS measure_name, COALESCE(s.hospitals_with_score, 0) AS hospitals_with_score, t.total_hospitals AS total_texas_hospitals, ROUND(100.0 * (t.total_hospitals - COALESCE(s.hospitals_with_score, 0)) / NULLIF(t.total_hospitals, 0), 1) AS percent_missing FROM hq.measures AS m CROSS JOIN total AS t LEFT JOIN scored AS s ON s.measure_id = UPPER(m.measure_id) WHERE t.total_hospitals - COALESCE(s.hospitals_with_score, 0) > t.total_hospitals / 2.0 ORDER BY percent_missing DESC, m.measure_id LIMIT 25

records.question: For Texas hospitals, compare the average 'would definitely recommend' percentage and the average overall star rating by ownership type. Count every Texas hospital of the type (even without a recommend score), keep only types with at least 5 hospitals, and list the highest average recommend percentage first.

answer.question: For Texas hospitals, compare the average 'would definitely recommend' percentage and the average overall star rating by ownership type. Count every Texas hospital of the type (even without a recommend score), keep only types with at least 5 hospitals, and list the highest average recommend percentage first.
answer.answer: Among Texas ownership types with at least 5 hospitals, the average “would definitely recommend” percentages are hospital averages, not patient counts; hospital counts include every hospital of that type, even those without a recommend score. Ordered from highest average recommend percentage: Government - Local — 11 hospitals, 79.0%, average overall rating 3.0 stars; Government - State — 15, 79.0%, 3.67 stars; Physician — 27, 78.85%, 3.67 stars; Government - Hospital District or Authority — 78, 75.73%, 2.77 stars; Voluntary non-profit - Other — 18, 74.36%, 3.43 stars; Veterans Health Administration — 5, 74.2%, 4.4 stars; Voluntary non-profit - Private — 134, 73.52%, 3.7 stars; Voluntary non-profit - Church — 5, 73.5%, 3.75 stars; Proprietary — 171, 68.58%, 3.01 stars.
answer.sql: SELECT h.hospital_ownership AS ownership_type, COUNT(*) AS texas_hospital_count, ROUND(CAST(AVG(c.top_box_pct) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS avg_would_definitely_recommend_pct, ROUND(CAST(AVG(h.overall_rating) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS avg_overall_star_rating FROM hq.hospitals AS h LEFT JOIN hq.v_hcahps AS c ON c.facility_id = h.facility_id AND UPPER(c.measure_id) = UPPER('H_RECMND_DY') WHERE UPPER(h.state) = UPPER('TX') GROUP BY h.hospital_ownership HAVING COUNT(*) >= 5 ORDER BY avg_would_definitely_recommend_pct DESC NULLS LAST, ownership_type LIMIT 200

answer.question: For the 'patients who rated the hospital 9 or 10' survey measure, do any Texas hospitals have scores from more than one reporting period (so a change from the prior period could be computed)? Give the number of Texas hospitals with a score, the largest number of reporting periods any one hospital has, and how many hospitals have more than one period.
answer.answer: For “patients who rated the hospital 9 or 10,” 297 Texas hospitals had a score. The largest number of reporting periods for any one hospital was 1, and 0 hospitals had more than one period. So, none had scores from multiple periods.
answer.sql: WITH hospital_periods AS (SELECT h.facility_id, COUNT(DISTINCT (mv.period_start, mv.period_end)) AS reporting_periods FROM hq.measure_values AS mv JOIN hq.hospitals AS h ON h.facility_id = mv.facility_id WHERE UPPER(mv.measure_id) = UPPER('H_HSP_RATING_9_10') AND h.state = 'TX' AND mv.score IS NOT NULL GROUP BY h.facility_id) SELECT m.measure_id, m.measure_name, COUNT(hp.facility_id) AS texas_hospitals_with_score, MAX(hp.reporting_periods) AS largest_reporting_period_count, COUNT(*) FILTER(WHERE hp.reporting_periods > 1) AS hospitals_with_multiple_periods FROM hospital_periods AS hp JOIN hq.measures AS m ON UPPER(m.measure_id) = UPPER('H_HSP_RATING_9_10') GROUP BY m.measure_id, m.measure_name LIMIT 200

answer.sql: WITH texas_z AS (SELECT facility_id, facility_name, county, measure_id, (score - AVG(score) OVER (PARTITION BY measure_id)) / NULLIF(STDDEV(score) OVER (PARTITION BY measure_id), 0) AS z_score FROM hq.v_tx_latest WHERE measure_id IN ('READM_30_PN', 'H_RECMND_DY', 'SEP_1') AND score IS NOT NULL), hospital_components AS (SELECT facility_id, facility_name, county, MAX(z_score) FILTER(WHERE measure_id = 'READM_30_PN') AS readm_z, MAX(z_score) FILTER(WHERE measure_id = 'H_RECMND_DY') AS recommend_z, MAX(z_score) FILTER(WHERE measure_id = 'SEP_1') AS sepsis_z FROM texas_z GROUP BY facility_id, facility_name, county HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT measure_id) = 3 AND COUNT(z_score) = 3), composites AS (SELECT facility_id, facility_name, county, -readm_z AS readm_higher_is_better_z, recommend_z, sepsis_z, (-readm_z + recommend_z + sepsis_z) / 3.0 AS composite_raw FROM hospital_components), ranked AS (SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY composite_raw DESC, UPPER(facility_name), UPPER(county)) AS highest_rank, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY composite_raw ASC, UPPER(facility_name), UPPER(county)) AS lowest_rank FROM composites), measure_labels AS (SELECT MAX(measure_name) FILTER(WHERE measure_id = 'READM_30_PN') AS readm_name, MAX(measure_name) FILTER(WHERE measure_id = 'H_RECMND_DY') AS recommend_name, MAX(measure_name) FILTER(WHERE measure_id = 'SEP_1') AS sepsis_name FROM hq.measures WHERE measure_id IN ('READM_30_PN', 'H_RECMND_DY', 'SEP_1')), selected AS (SELECT 1 AS group_order, 'Highest' AS composite_group, highest_rank AS group_rank, facility_id, facility_name, county, readm_higher_is_better_z, recommend_z, sepsis_z, composite_raw FROM ranked WHERE highest_rank <= 10 UNION ALL SELECT 2 AS group_order, 'Lowest' AS composite_group, lowest_rank AS group_rank, facility_id, facility_name, county, readm_higher_is_better_z, recommend_z, sepsis_z, composite_raw FROM ranked WHERE lowest_rank <= 10) SELECT composite_group, group_rank, facility_id, facility_name, county, 'READM_30_PN' AS readmission_measure_id, measure_labels.readm_name AS readmission_measure_name, ROUND(readm_higher_is_better_z, 2) AS readmission_z_flipped, 'H_RECMND_DY' AS recommend_measure_id, measure_labels.recommend_name AS recommend_measure_name, ROUND(recommend_z, 2) AS recommend_z, 'SEP_1' AS sepsis_measure_id, measure_labels.sepsis_name AS sepsis_measure_name, ROUND(sepsis_z, 2) AS sepsis_z, ROUND(composite_raw, 2) AS composite FROM selected CROSS JOIN measure_labels ORDER BY group_order, CASE WHEN group_order = 1 THEN composite_raw END DESC, CASE WHEN group_order = 2 THEN composite_raw END ASC, UPPER(facility_name), UPPER(county) LIMIT 200

answer.sql: WITH ranked_rates AS (SELECT mv.facility_id, mv.measure_id, mv.score, mv.denominator, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY mv.facility_id, mv.measure_id ORDER BY mv.period_end DESC NULLS LAST, mv.period_start DESC NULLS LAST) AS period_rank FROM hq.measure_values AS mv WHERE UPPER(mv.measure_id) = UPPER('READM_30_PN')), latest_rates AS (SELECT facility_id, score, denominator FROM ranked_rates WHERE period_rank = 1) SELECT h.county, COUNT(*) AS number_of_hospitals, COUNT(lr.score) AS hospitals_with_rate, m.measure_id, m.measure_name, ROUND(CAST(AVG(lr.score) FILTER(WHERE lr.score IS NOT NULL) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS plain_mean_rate, ROUND(CAST((SUM(lr.score * lr.denominator) FILTER(WHERE lr.score IS NOT NULL AND lr.denominator IS NOT NULL AND lr.denominator > 0) / NULLIF(SUM(lr.denominator) FILTER(WHERE lr.score IS NOT NULL AND lr.denominator IS NOT NULL AND lr.denominator > 0), 0)) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS discharge_weighted_mean_rate FROM hq.hospitals AS h LEFT JOIN latest_rates AS lr ON lr.facility_id = h.facility_id CROSS JOIN hq.measures AS m WHERE UPPER(h.state) = UPPER('TX') AND h.county IS NOT NULL AND UPPER(m.measure_id) = UPPER('READM_30_PN') GROUP BY h.county, m.measure_id, m.measure_name HAVING COUNT(lr.score) >= 3 ORDER BY discharge_weighted_mean_rate ASC, h.county ASC LIMIT 200

records.question: For six measures, what share of Texas hospitals do better than the national average (average over all U.S. hospitals with a score)? Measures: 30-day pneumonia readmission rate, 30-day heart failure death rate, central-line infection ratio (lower is better for these three), sepsis care percentage, 'would definitely recommend' percentage and HCAHPS summary star rating (higher is better for these three). Return measure ID, the national average (2 decimals), Texas hospitals with a score, how many beat the national average and the share in percent (1 decimal), highest share first, ties by measure ID.

answer.question: For six measures, what share of Texas hospitals do better than the national average (average over all U.S. hospitals with a score)? Measures: 30-day pneumonia readmission rate, 30-day heart failure death rate, central-line infection ratio (lower is better for these three), sepsis care percentage, 'would definitely recommend' percentage and HCAHPS summary star rating (higher is better for these three). Return measure ID, the national average (2 decimals), Texas hospitals with a score, how many beat the national average and the share in percent (1 decimal), highest share first, ties by measure ID.
answer.answer:
Shares are ordered highest first. National averages are averages across U.S. hospitals with a score for each measure, not patient counts; Texas hospitals beat the average using the stated lower- or higher-is-better direction.
- HAI_1_SIR (central-line infection ratio; lower is better): national average 0.58; 151 Texas hospitals with a score; 99 beat the average; share 65.6%.
- MORT_30_HF (30-day heart failure death rate; lower is better): national average 11.07; 206 Texas hospitals with a score; 132 beat the average; share 64.1%.
- SEP_1 (sepsis care percentage; higher is better): national average 63.79; 233 Texas hospitals with a score; 146 beat the average; share 62.7%.
- READM_30_PN (30-day pneumonia readmission rate; lower is better): national average 17.34; 258 Texas hospitals with a score; 150 beat the average; share 58.1%.
- H_RECMND_DY (would definitely recommend percentage; higher is better): national average 71.22; 297 Texas hospitals with a score; 158 beat the average; share 53.2%.
- H_STAR_RATING (HCAHPS summary star rating; higher is better): national average 3.27; 229 Texas hospitals with a score; 92 beat the average; share 40.2%.
answer.sql: WITH latest_rows AS (SELECT mv.facility_id, mv.measure_id, mv.measure_name, mv.score, h.state, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY mv.facility_id, mv.measure_id ORDER BY mv.period_end DESC, mv.period_start DESC) AS rn FROM hq.measure_values AS mv JOIN hq.hospitals AS h ON h.facility_id = mv.facility_id WHERE UPPER(mv.measure_id) IN ('READM_30_PN', 'MORT_30_HF', 'HAI_1_SIR', 'SEP_1', 'H_RECMND_DY', 'H_STAR_RATING')), scored_latest AS (SELECT facility_id, measure_id, measure_name, score, state FROM latest_rows WHERE rn = 1 AND score IS NOT NULL), national_averages AS (SELECT measure_id, AVG(score) AS national_avg FROM scored_latest GROUP BY measure_id), texas_comparison AS (SELECT t.measure_id, MAX(t.measure_name) AS measure_name, n.national_avg, COUNT(*) AS texas_hospitals_with_score, COUNT(*) FILTER(WHERE (t.measure_id IN ('READM_30_PN', 'MORT_30_HF', 'HAI_1_SIR') AND t.score < n.national_avg) OR (t.measure_id IN ('SEP_1', 'H_RECMND_DY', 'H_STAR_RATING') AND t.score > n.national_avg)) AS texas_hospitals_beat_national FROM scored_latest AS t JOIN national_averages AS n ON n.measure_id = t.measure_id WHERE t.state = 'TX' GROUP BY t.measure_id, n.national_avg) SELECT measure_id, measure_name, ROUND(CAST(national_avg AS DECIMAL), 2) AS national_average, texas_hospitals_with_score, texas_hospitals_beat_national, ROUND(CAST(texas_hospitals_beat_national AS DECIMAL) * 100 / NULLIF(texas_hospitals_with_score, 0), 1) AS share_percent FROM texas_comparison ORDER BY share_percent DESC, measure_id LIMIT 200
